paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 (expressed as a percentage) on geometry problems (Geomverse) and the number of child nodes (tree width) for rollout search, comparing two large vision-language models: GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis, labeled “Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width),” is linearly scaled and ranges from 1 to 7, with tick marks at integer values. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)”, is also linearly scaled, ranging from 15 to 35, with major gridlines every 5 units. The GPT-4o model is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers: it begins at 24.4% accuracy at tree width 1, rises to 28.9% at width 3, peaks at 34.4% at width 5, and then declines to 31.1% at width 7. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet model is shown as a dashed light purple line with ‘x’ markers: it starts at 26.7% at width 1, increases slightly to 27.8% at width 3, then decreases to 24.4% at width 5, and further drops to 20.0% at width 7. Both models exhibit an inverted U-shaped performance trend relative to tree width, with GPT-4o achieving higher peak accuracy and maintaining better performance across wider trees.
